messages.content:
You are the Solution Architect of a platform that adds new functionality to an application that already works. You
receive the approved user stories of the request (with their acceptance criteria), the inventory of the existing
application read by code (its endpoints with their fields, its tables and its service methods) and its code. You
design only the delta: the smallest set of changes that delivers every story while reusing what exists. A person
approves it at gate C3 before any code is written.

Rules of the delta:
- Each change has a `name` (PascalCase, e.g. PaymentStatusQuery), a `description`, and the `stories` it delivers
  (every story of the request must be in a change).
- A change that exposes behaviour has `http_method` and `path` (lowercase, under the application's existing API
  prefix), with the `request` and `response` fields (`name`, `type`). A new endpoint never takes the method and path
  of an existing one; to extend an existing endpoint, keep its method and path and list what it `reuses`.
- `reuses`: the names of existing classes the change builds on (exactly as in the code, e.g. PaymentService).
- `tables`: the existing tables the change reads or writes (exactly as in the inventory). `new_tables`: tables it
  needs that do not exist (avoid them unless a story requires data the application does not keep).
- `files`: the paths of the files you expect the change to create or modify, under src/main/java. Never an existing
  test, never the build file: the delta only uses libraries the application already has.
- Follow the application's layering: controllers delegate to services; SQL stays where the application keeps it.
- `decisions`: what a reviewer must know (transactions, errors, compatibility with existing clients).

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else, with this shape:
{"changes": [{"name": "...", "description": "...", "stories": ["US-001"], "http_method": "GET", "path": "/...",
  "request": [{"name": "...", "type": "..."}], "response": [{"name": "...", "type": "..."}], "reuses": ["..."],
  "tables": ["..."], "new_tables": [], "files": ["src/main/java/..."]}],
 "decisions": [{"title": "...", "decision": "..."}]}

response.content: {"changes":[{"name":"OrderStatusQuery","description":"Read-only query for the status of a company's payment order. It looks the order up by its key (order_no, company_id) in the orders table and returns the stored status, trimmed because the column is CHAR(1): P for pending, A for paid. If the order does not exist for that company it answers 404 (not found). It runs a single SELECT. It does not call CoreBankingClient, does not run any UPDATE and does not touch accounts or fees, so nothing is debited or modified.","stories":["US-001"],"http_method":"GET","path":"/api/v1/companies/{companyId}/orders/{orderId}","request":[{"name":"companyId","type":"Integer"},{"name":"orderId","type":"Integer"}],"response":[{"name":"orderId","type":"Integer"},{"name":"companyId","type":"Integer"},{"name":"status","type":"String"}],"reuses":[],"tables":["orders"],"new_tables":[],"files":["src/main/java/com/contoso/billpay/api/OrderController.java","src/main/java/com/contoso/billpay/api/OrderStatusResponse.java","src/main/java/com/contoso/billpay/domain/OrderService.java"]}],"decisions":[{"title":"Separate controller and service, existing payment flow untouched","decision":"The query goes in a new OrderController and OrderService, following the existing layering: the controller delegates to the service, and the SQL lives in a domain service that uses JdbcTemplate, as in PaymentService. PaymentController, PaymentService and POST /api/v1/payments are not modified, so existing clients and PaymentServiceTest are unaffected. The new GET path does not collide with any existing endpoint."},{"title":"Status values and 'not found' response","decision":"The service returns Optional<String> with the trimmed status from the orders table. It returns P and A as stored, with no mapping. The controller answers 200 with {orderId, companyId, status} when the order exists and 404 with no body when it does not. The channel tells 'not found' apart from the P and A states by HTTP code, and no business error code is added to the 5000x range used by payments."},{"title":"No side effects, no transaction needed","decision":"The method executes one SELECT status FROM orders WHERE order_no = ? AND company_id = ?, on the full primary key. It has no writes and no dependency on CoreBankingClient, which guarantees the 'consulta sin efectos' criterion. No explicit transaction is required. The unit test can check this with ScriptedJdbc.executed: it must contain no UPDATE, and the service is built without a core client."}]}
